- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of the 30-day window).
- Forecasts show a strong upward trend that fails to account for sharp downward corrections after spikes (e.g., 74+ → 70–72).
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: after a spike, it continues rising instead of correcting downward.
- Overshoot occurs after high peaks: model forecasts remain elevated even after true values drop sharply.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to capture volatility or sudden drops in the last 5–10 days of the window.
- Model underreacts to recent low values; fails to adjust downward when true values are trending lower.
- Horizon-specific error: forecasts for 30-day ahead are too optimistic and fail to reflect short-term volatility or policy-driven corrections.
